lesson.title: Hoeveel Kost Het?
lesson.subtitle: prices, paying and the Dutch pin machine

hook.title: How Much, and How to Pay
hook.content: Hoeveel kost het? Ik wil betalen. Ik pin hier. Shopping Dutch is a handful of frames: ask the price, state the payment, choose cash or card.

pattern.title: Kost, betalen, pinnen
pattern.content: Hoeveel kost het? Het kost tien euro. Ik wil betalen. Ik pin hier. Pinnen is the everyday verb for paying by card; betalen is the general verb.
pattern.trap_note: Kost is the third-person form of kosten. Do not say hoeveel kosten het for one item; use kost.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Hoeveel Kost Het?):
exercises.target_answer: hoeveel, kosten, het geld, de euro, betalen, pinnen
exercises.meaning: how much; how many, to cost, money, euro, to pay, to pay by card
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Hoeveel Kost Het?": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “How much does it cost?”?
exercises.explanation: “Hoeveel kost het?” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Hoeveel Kost Het?”.

cues: It means: I want to pay.
exercises.explanation: “Ik wil betalen.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Kost, betalen, pinnen.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Kost is the third-person form of kosten. Do not say hoeveel kosten het for one item; use kost.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Ik pin hier.” is word-for-word “I pin here.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Kost, betalen, pinnen.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: It costs ten euros.
exercises.explanation: “Het kost tien euro.” reuses only material taught in “Hoeveel Kost Het?” — Kost, betalen, pinnen.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Het kost tien euro.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Kost, betalen, pinnen.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I have no money.”
twist.explanation: Geen negates the indefinite noun geld; hebben stays positive.

summary.outcome: Ask prices and complete a simple payment exchange.
summary.takeaway: Shopping is a small set of frames; the currency is the only variable.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Werkte Je Niet?.

hoeveel.etymology_derivation: hoe + veel ('how much'), transparent in Dutch.

kosten.etymology_derivation: English cost and Dutch kosten are the same verb.

geld.etymology_derivation: English geld is archaic; Dutch geld is everyday money.

betalen.etymology_derivation: The old sense of tell was 'count'; betalen is literally to settle a count.

pinnen.etymology_derivation: From the PIN of a bank card; Dutch turned the acronym into a verb.
